The body has two pressure languages that may disagree. value.claim: Potentially false or misleading claims: (1) The README says '107 Lua test suites plus mortality, expected-red QA, and live-substrate smoke programs.' The current_state.md says 'lua tests/run.lua 107 suites passed.' But the release closure notes say 'ordinary Lua suite is green' without specifying count. The inventory shows ~90 production modules; 107 test suites may include duplicates or legacy tests. (2) The README claims 'full-tree route authority with legacy retained only as read-only instrumentation' but the edge evidence shows only 6/22 edges executed. 'Full-tree' is misleading when 15 edges have no executed direction. (3) The current_state.md claims 'The first repository hand chapter is complete' but the hand can only create one absent UTF-8 text file. It cannot patch, overwrite, delete, rename, mkdir, search/read arbitrary files, run tests or git, or coordinate a multi-file transaction.

value.claim: Unsafe authority boundaries: (1) The command sandbox must become capability-based before arbitrary hands are connected. (2) The CLI can widen authority if hostile arguments are not properly filtered. (3) The default legacy router cannot select CONNECT or DISSOLVE, but tree mode can. If tree mode becomes default before all 22 edges are tested, the body could make unsafe routing decisions. (4) The qualified pressure system has uncalibrated coefficients (all 1) and is marked vibed_control. If promoted to default without calibration, it could make incorrect routing decisions.
